summary: THE ARM IS RETIRE, AND THE TWO OTHER ARMS WERE DISPROVED BY DRIVING BEFORE IT WAS TAKEN. src/tok/api.py::build_vocabulary's `_drop = float(tok.dropout)` / `if not 0.0 <= _drop <= 1.0` is deleted; the interval ruling now lives only on `domain=(0.0, 1.0)` at src/tok/levers.py::TOKLevers, and everything the clause argued and measured moved there. THE ENDPOINT QUESTION WAS SETTLED FIRST AND IT DOES NOT BITE: `not 0.0 <= x <= 1.0` ACCEPTS both 0.0 and 1.0, and a CLOSED [0.0, 1.0] accepts both, so this is not the OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC one-point disagreement -- it is pre-emption. WHICH RULE IS WIDER: NEITHER. 22 values per arm from -1e9 to 1e26 (including -0.0, -1e-320, 1e-320, -1e-09, 0.9999999999999999, 1.0, 1.0000000000000002, nan, inf, -inf), one fresh process per cell, through a real spine.assemble.build and a real TOK.build_vocabulary, first on the shipped tree and again with the pair NEUTRALISED in a copy of src/ outside the repository so the clause answered alone: 22 of 22 cells IDENTICAL in verdict. Unlike OPT's twelfth refusal the clause gains nothing from the other arm of the finiteness switch either -- with REFUSE_NON_FINITE_FLOAT=False and the pair gone, TOK's own GENERATED sweep over tok.keys() refuses nan/inf/-inf by name -- so it was dead in BOTH arms. THE DISCRIMINATOR: what the clause knew is a property OF THE NUMBER, namely that the draw it is compared against, `stream.random() < dropout`, runs on [0.0, 1.0), so at or below 0.0 nothing is ever skipped and at or above 1.0 everything is. Nothing it knew depended on another lever, an arm or a mechanism. ONE RETIRED SENTENCE IS RECORDED CORRECTED, NOT REQUOTED, exactly as OPT found: the clause justified its interval as following from 'it is declared as units.PROBABILITY ... and a probability is not outside [0, 1]' -- the unit label -- which is the inference THIS VERY FILE rules against for `mint_novel` ('will be surprised by 2.0, which is legal'). The conclusion was right and the stated reason was the wrong one; the declaration carries the argument from the DRAW instead, and the file now says in as many words that nothing about this pair extends to `mint_pmin` (U.PROBABILITY, no domain) or `mint_novel` (U.FRACTION, an exponent, no domain) by proximity, and that a reader who wants a domain elsewhere in the file must produce a comparison and not a unit. A SECOND ROTTED SENTENCE WAS FOUND WHILE IT COULD STILL PRINT, in build_vocabulary's own docstring, and it is corrected rather than deleted. TWO NEW MEASUREMENTS WENT ONTO THE DECLARATION AND THEY ARE THE reason the closed top end is right: TOK_DROPOUT=0.9999999999999999 is BIT-FOR-BIT what 1.0 does (size 323, mint 67, refused 67, dropout_skip 22374, three regularized calls returning ONE answer of 10000 ids), so the damage is already complete at the largest float BELOW the endpoint and an exclusive end would have bought nothing; and TOK_DROPOUT=1e-320 attaches the stream and records tok.dropout_skip 0 rather than ABSENT, which is armed-but-0 against the default's UNREACHABLE. THE tok.dropout.mint REPAIR IS UNTOUCHED AND STILL HOLDS: all three `rng_for("tok.dropout.mint", seed)` sites are byte-identical in the diff, and three tokenize(regularize=True) calls give 3 of 3 distinct segmentations at 0.3 and at 0.5. NOTHING IS NOW SAFE OR BOUNDED: TOK_DROPOUT=1.0 still builds and still switches the tokenizer off, and the three other TOK float levers have no interval at all. O15 no longer names any TOK lever; suite is ownership 15+70 0 failing, contract 16+77 0, census 8 0, assemble 9 0, couplings 4 0, fabric 9 0, derive 575 oracle cases 0.

findings.item: THE ENDPOINT TEST, RUN FIRST: `not 0.0 <= _drop <= 1.0` and the CLOSED pair [0.0, 1.0] agree exactly at 0.0 and at 1.0, so the 'neither retire nor drop' third possibility does not apply
findings.detail: The brief names this as the thing to disprove before touching anything, with OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC as the live example where a half-open clause refuses the 1.0 its closed pair admits. TOK_DROPOUT's clause is an INVERTED CHAIN that is inclusive at BOTH ends -- `not 0.0 <= x <= 1.0` refuses exactly (-inf, 0.0) U (1.0, inf) and accepts 0.0 and 1.0 -- and `domain=(0.0, 1.0)` is closed at both ends and admits exactly [0.0, 1.0]. Established by driving, not by reading the operators: both endpoints BUILD under the pair and BUILD again with the pair neutralised, and both floating-point neighbours (1.0000000000000002 above, -1e-09 and -1e-320 below) are REFUSED under either layer. -0.0 builds under both, which is the value that separates a `< 0.0` clause from a `<= 0.0` one and separates nothing here. So this is pre-emption, not a one-point disagreement, and the fork is real.

findings.item: THE RETIRED CLAUSE'S STATED REASON WAS THE U.FRACTION MISTAKE IN THIS FILE'S OWN COSTUME, AND IT IS RECORDED CORRECTED RATHER THAN REQUOTED
findings.detail: The clause argued the interval this way: 'It is declared as units.PROBABILITY and as the Probability of skipping an available merge ... a probability is not outside [0, 1]'. That is an inference FROM THE UNIT LABEL, and src/tok/levers.py is one of the three files carrying this tree's standing ruling AGAINST it: `mint_novel` says a reader who takes 'fraction 0..1' as a bound on legal values 'will be surprised by 2.0, which is legal'. Carrying that sentence onto the declaration unexamined would have put the U.FRACTION mistake beside the ruling that forbids it. The conclusion was nonetheless right, for a different reason -- the DRAW, not the label -- and the declaration says so. THE RULING STANDS AND THE FILE SAYS SO LOUDER THAN BEFORE: a new paragraph on the dropout declaration states that nothing about this pair extends to its neighbours by proximity, names `mint_pmin` (U.PROBABILITY, NO domain) and `mint_novel` (a dimensionless exponent wearing U.FRACTION, NO domain) as the two levers a reader would wrongly generalise to, gives the counts (75 U.FRACTION and 5 U.PROBABILITY in this tree, a handful with pairs), and requires anyone adding a domain elsewhere in the file to produce a COMPARISON rather than a unit. This lever earned its pair by being compared against a bounded draw on every counting segmentation; that is an argument about arithmetic and it does not transfer.

AND THAT RULING STANDS UNCHANGED ... NOTHING ABOUT THIS DECLARATION EXTENDS TO ITS NEIGHBOURS BY PROXIMITY' and 'ONE SENTENCE OF THE RETIRED CLAUSE IS RECORDED CORRECTED RATHER THAN REQUOTED'. `mint_novel`'s own paragraph is unchanged: 'a reader who takes "fraction 0..1" as a bound on legal values will be surprised by 2.0, which is legal.' tests/test_census.py: '=== 8 checks + the self-test, 0 failing ==='.

findings.item: TWO NEW MEASUREMENTS THAT ARE THE ARGUMENT FOR THE CLOSED TOP END: 0.9999999999999999 is bit-for-bit what 1.0 does, and 1e-320 is armed-but-0 rather than unreachable
findings.detail: The brief asks whether 1.0 is a value the tokenizer can actually run and whether `> 1.0` or `>= 1.0` is the rule that agrees with the pair. It runs, and neither one-sided rule would have been right, because THE DAMAGE IS NOT AT THE ENDPOINT. Driven on a 10000-byte two-area sample: at 0.9999999999999999 -- the largest float below 1.0 -- the build, the counters and all three regularized segmentations are identical in every printed number to 1.0, because random() has 53 bits and a draw at or above that value is never seen. An EXCLUSIVE top end would therefore have refused a legally typed setting and bought nothing measurable, which is the whole case for the pair being CLOSED at 1.0 rather than the case for refusing it. At the other end, TOK_DROPOUT=1e-320 builds bit-identically to 0.0 (size 334, mint 78) but attaches the stream, because the guard is `> 0`, and the ledger then carries tok.dropout_skip 0 instead of ABSENT -- armed-but-0 against the shipped default's UNREACHABLE, which is the middle of the three DID IT FIRE states and a distinction this package's own convention depends on. Both are now on the declaration.

TOK_DROPOUT=1.0 still BUILDS and still switches the tokenizer off -- every available merge skipped, bytes_per_token collapsing, the segmentation deterministic again and the knob reading on -- and so does 0.9999999999999999.
